question: If the lengths of two sides of an isosceles triangle are 6 cm and 12 cm, then find the length of the third side.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an isosceles triangle, two sides are equal, so the third side is either 6 cm or 12 cm.

According to the triangle inequality theorem, the sum of any two sides must be strictly greater than the third side.

If sides are 6 cm, 6 cm, and 12 cm: 6 + 6 = 12 (not greater than 12, so it is invalid).

If sides are 12 cm, 12 cm, and 6 cm: 12 + 6 = 18 > 12 (satisfies the condition, so it is valid).

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**
